output.reason: Small, localized, non-spreading itchy rash on the forearm beginning after gardening fits a localized contact reaction; no reported systemic or airway symptoms and no reported functional impairment or treatment failure, so no clinician task is required now.
output.patientMessage: You can manage this at home for now: wash the area and any clothing that touched the plants, keep the skin cool and moisturized, and avoid scratching; a pharmacist can advise on over-the-counter options for itch. See a clinician if the rash spreads well beyond the contact area, blisters or weeps, becomes painful, warm or feverish, or isn't settling. If you develop throat tightness, facial swelling or trouble breathing, call 911.
differential: Contact dermatitis from plant or garden irritant at the contact site
Localized allergic (type IV) reaction, e.g. urushiol exposure
